key_insight: Human and LLM-generated synthesis recipes performed similarly, and their closed-loop collaboration led to the discovery of a new material prototype, Ba3PtO5.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that AI can accelerate materials synthesis planning, but experimental validation remains essential for turning generated candidates into real discoveries.
method: Compared human-written and LLM-written synthesis recipes for known and unknown materials in the Ruddlesden-Popper phase space.
Tested each recipe in the lab and fed success/failure results back into a closed-loop collaboration process.
Used two rounds of evaluation to compare performance and refine the human-LLM interaction.
evidence_signal: Recipe success rates were reported for known and unknown materials across two rounds, with humans and LLMs showing comparable performance and producing a new discovered compound, Ba3PtO5.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply on unknown materials, so relying on LLM-generated synthesis without robust experimental feedback could lead to low success rates.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
